commands.name: new
usage: delulu new       <name> [--lib] [--json]   (a package that already checks, tests and runs;
its declared ceiling is exactly what its code does — one effect for a bin, none for a lib)

commands.name: check
usage: delulu check     <file.delulu>... | <package-dir> [--locked] [--json]   (several files in ONE process:
the per-invocation floor dominates a small check — see measurements/agent-loop/RECORD.md)

commands.name: fix
usage: delulu fix       <file.delulu> [--dry-run] [--json] [--accept-widening <repair-id>]...
(applies the checker's own typed repairs; a repair that would WIDEN what the program
may do is never applied unless you name it, and there is no accept-all flag)

commands.name: fmt
usage: delulu fmt     <file-or-dir>... [--check] [--json] | --stdin | --migrate 0.7 <file-or-dir>...
(one canonical style, zero options; --check exits 1 on unformatted; unparseable files are refused)

commands.name: test
usage: delulu test      [paths|patterns]... [--json] [--seed N]   (authority-isolated tests; each holds only its declared, ceiling-bounded row)
[--test-authority 'effects = ["Write"]']..  (a ceiling in the manifest's [test-authority] syntax:
inside a package it may only narrow the package's; for a file outside one it is the only ceiling)

commands.name: lsp
usage: delulu lsp       (LSP 3.17 over stdio — one server for every editor and agent IDE; analysis only)

commands.name: keygen
usage: delulu keygen    [--name N] [--json]                 (mint an ed25519 signing key in ~/.delulu/keys)

commands.name: sign
usage: delulu sign      <artifact> [--hybrid] [--unstable] [--json]

commands.name: verify-sig
usage: delulu verify-sig <artifact> [--key HEX] [--require-hybrid] [--unstable] [--json]
(detached .sig over .dwx/.dpx/tarballs; --hybrid/--require-hybrid touch post-quantum
ML-DSA-65 and need --unstable — unaudited, pre-KAT, refused as DL1910 without it)

commands.name: publish
usage: delulu publish   --dry-run <pkg-dir> [--index DIR] [--json]   (validate manifest + semver-authority + signature; no upload)

commands.name: deploy
usage: delulu deploy    plan --service NAME=PKG_DIR --env ENVFILE.toml [--json]   (check each service's effects and requests against the environment profile;
DL1909 when one exceeds it, naming the call — scopes decided as `authority --within` decides them)

commands.name: add
usage: delulu add       <pkg> --index DIR                   (resolve + show authority from the index line, no download)
delulu add       --path <dir> [--accept-authority] [--json]   (declare a dependency on the package
beside yours; the pin is COMPUTED from it, and a dependency that needs an effect is
shown and refused until you accept it — granting authority stays a person's decision)

commands.name: login
usage: delulu login     --registry URL --token VALUE [--json] (store a scoped publish token; never echoed)

commands.name: build
usage: delulu build     <package-dir> [--locked] [--deny-advisories] [--advisory-feed F] [--json]   (resolve deps + verify pins/authority)
delulu build     <file.delulu|package-dir> --target wasm [-o out.dwx]  (emit an authority-carrying .dwx)

commands.name: lock
usage: delulu lock      [package-dir] [--accept-authority <pkg>]... [--json]

commands.name: run
usage: delulu run       <file.delulu | package-dir | file.dwx> [--json] [--grant K[=V]]... [--grant-manifest] [--no-prompt]
(a package-dir runs a MULTI-PACKAGE program: the graph is checked, then flattened
for execution; two modules declaring the same top-level name are refused, not guessed — D61)
[--grant plugin=PATH]  (P2/D-V2-27: where a program may LOAD a plugin artifact from. Paths go
through the containment resolver, so `..`, a symlink or a case difference cannot widen it; a
package may narrow it further with `[plugins] allow = ["<blake3>"]` in delulu.toml)
[--trace-effects] [--trace-out F] [--assert-trace] [--seed N] [--clock fixed:MS]
[--sandbox | --sandbox=off] [--sandbox-profile dev|contained|hostile-agent] [--limits mem=N,cpu=S,wall=S]
[--break-glass TICKET]  (PS-B-06: on a host whose operator requires the sandbox, a ticket they
signed lets this ONE program run once without it — loud, audited, and relaxing nothing else)
(every run is budgeted: 1 GiB of memory and 5 minutes of processor time unless --limits sets
others — never zero, never unlimited (D-V2-25); a run that spends one is stopped, and the
report's outcome.stopped_by says which)
[--mode strict|audit]  (audit performs NOTHING: it reports the policy that would hold and the
grants the program would need — the dry run to read before letting unfamiliar code run)
(--sandbox runs the program as a jailed guest holding no authority of its own: the host
performs every effect under the same checks. A surface the channel does not carry yet is
REFUSED, never quietly run unconfined; --limits may narrow a profile, never widen it)
(PS-A-10: --mode and --sandbox-profile are REFUSED without --sandbox rather than
ignored, and a command line saying both --sandbox and --sandbox=off is refused in either order)
[--report-out F]  (the runtime writes the run report there — sandbox level, mode, outcome —
in every outcome; never on stdout, which the program could forge; refused inside a writable grant)
[--engine wasm]  (run `main` on the WebAssembly backend instead of the interpreter)
[--broker embedded|daemon] [--epoch-ms N]  (custody: daemon routes ops through the broker)
[--lease TOKEN]  (run under a delegated lease — the authority is the delegated node's)
[--isolation none|process|microvm]  (process isolates FOREIGN code only — the program stays in-process;
microvm runs the program as a guest in its own kernel: Linux+KVM+a guest image; elsewhere DL1408)
[--sandbox-backend external:CMD]  (L3, with --sandbox: the operator's launcher — Docker + gVisor, Kata,
a cloud sandbox, ssh — runs `delulu __guest --stdio-pipes` in THEIR environment on its stdin/stdout;
the level is labelled external and its guarantees unknown — DeluluLang measures none of them)
[--require-attestation HEX]  (PS-D-02, with external: only: the launcher's attester must sign a statement
over this run's nonce with this pinned ed25519 key, or the program is never sent; its claims are
reported as the attester's, never as the host's — `delulu sandbox attest` is a software attester)
[--launcher-digest HEX]  (PS-E-04, with external: only: the launcher's file must have this BLAKE3 digest —
the `launcher_blake3` every external run reports — or nothing is started)
[--actors-threads N] [--on-quiesce report] [--on-actor-death abort] [--debug-rcaps]  (Stage 7 actors)
[--foreign-isolation inproc|process] [--foreign-max-ret BYTES] [--trace-memory] [--adapter-record DIR]
[--broker-profile sim|hw:ADAPTER] [--sim-step MS] [--signoff F] [--approved F]  (devices: sim is deterministic under --seed;
hw needs the sign-off record of the artifact simulation approved — DL1905;
--sim-step MS makes sim lease timing deterministic per interaction, independent of build speed — D20;
--adapter-cmd CMD names the hw driver: a signature beside it that does NOT verify always refuses,
and --require-signed-adapter refuses an unsigned one — D52;
--adapter-artifact PATH names WHICH bytes were signed (an interpreter-hosted driver
names the interpreter in --adapter-cmd, not the driver), and --adapter-signer HEX pins
the key: unpinned, a `.sig` beside the driver proves only that SOMEBODY signed it — D53;
--adapter-dpx FILE --adapter-transport CMD --adapter-signer HEX: the driver's LOGIC as a signed
Verified plugin, read once, pinned, re-proved and interpreted by the host; CMD only carries its
frames to the device and the replies back — P8-02;
a driver (or transport) prints READY before its first command, within --adapter-startup-ms MS
(default 10000, at most 120000); silence or any other first line refuses the run — RW 4.19)

commands.name: plugin
usage: delulu plugin    build <package-dir> [-o out.dpx] [--sign keyfile] [--json]   (a `kind = "plugin"` package → .dpx)
delulu plugin    inspect <file.dpx> [--json]   (manifest, class, exports, section hashes, signature)
delulu plugin    verify  <file.dpx> [--json]   (load steps 1,2,5 — identical verdicts to a real load)

commands.name: authority
usage: delulu authority <file.delulu | package-dir> [--grants] [--json]
[--broker embedded|daemon] [--foreign-isolation inproc|process] [--isolation none|process|microvm]  (labels on the report)
delulu authority <file.delulu> --within <grant>... | --within-file <file> [--json]
(P9-01: is everything the program asks for inside this boundary? within (exit 0), or exceeds /
unsupported / inconclusive (exit 1) with each request named and the call that makes it. The
boundary is in the --grant grammar and is checked against, never granted)
delulu authority --diff <old.lock> <new.lock-or-package-dir> [--json]

commands.name: why
usage: delulu why       <Effect> <file.delulu | package-dir> [--json]

commands.name: atlas
usage: delulu atlas     <file.delulu | package-dir> [--format tree|digest|json|dot|mermaid|html]
(mermaid is a MODULE-LEVEL overview — no functions/effects; dot|json|tree show the whole graph)
[--out DIR] [--budget N] [--gods N] [--custody] [--json]
delulu atlas     node <name-or-id> | callers <fn> | calls <fn> | why <Effect|resource> [target] [--json] [--budget N]
delulu atlas     path <A> <B> [target] [--json]   (a typed, deterministic code + authority graph)
delulu atlas     chain [target] [--sandbox-profile P] [--json]   (the V2 chain, one view: program →
authority → effects → capabilities → sandbox policy → resources → plugins →
actors → devices → execution boundary)

commands.name: repl
usage: delulu repl      [--grant K[=V]]...

commands.name: audit
usage: delulu audit     tail [N] | query [--node g_ID] [--action A] [--effect E] | verify
[--dir DIR] [--json]  (default DIR: $DELULU_STATE_DIR/audit, else ~/.delulu/audit)
delulu audit     bundle [--out F] | reconcile <bundle> [--expect-start HASH]  [--dir DIR] [--json]
delulu audit     export --format ocsf [--since SEQ] [--out F] [--device-name NAME]  [--dir DIR] [--json]
(the chain as OCSF 1.8.0 events, each carrying its record) | verify --ocsf F [--expect-start HASH]

commands.name: grants
usage: delulu grants    list | tree | inspect <g_ID> | revoke <g_ID>  [--json]
delulu grants    delegate [--parent g_ID] --effects E,.. [--fs-read P].. [--fs-write P]..
[--net H].. [--secret N].. [--secret-to N@HOST[:PORT]].. [--declassify N]..
[--device DEV:dim=lo..hi,..].. [--ttl 1h] [--budget mem=N,cpu=S] [--multi] [--owner CODE]
(prints a lease token; a budget left unnamed is the parent's, and a `run --lease` is held to it;
a secret is sent only to the origins its `--secret-to` names — none is nowhere)
delulu grants    certify --subject HEX --effects E,.. [--fs-read ABS].. [--fs-write ABS].. [--net H]..
[--device D].. --ttl 20m [--key F] [--parent-cert F] [--out F]
delulu grants    adopt <cert>.. [--anchor HEX].. | pubkey [--key F]   (federation: mint offline, adopt locally)
delulu grants    receipt --for FINGERPRINT --ttl 1h [--key F] [--out F] | renew <receipt> [--anchor HEX]..
delulu grants    diff <old.grants> <new.grants> | diff <g_OLD> <g_NEW>   (P9-02: what a change of authority ADDS —
effect, scope, special-use, device and budget reach; two grant files, one grant a line, or two
lease nodes through their broker; exit 1 when it adds any, 0 when none)
delulu grants    propose <report.json> [--node g_ID]   (P9-03: the narrowest grant for the call a refused run was
refused at, from its `run --report-out` report and the program's source — that call's own requirement;
exit 1 when there is none to propose, and why; with `--node`, FILED with the broker as the request of
that node — the one the refused run held — and nothing is granted until it is approved)
delulu grants    proposals | approve <pp_ID> --parent g_ID [--ttl 1h] [--owner CODE] | reject <pp_ID> --reason ".."
(an approval delegates, under the approver's own node, the proposer's authority and what it asked —
bounded by ⊑, so a node cannot approve its own widening — and prints a lease token for the re-run;
a rejection's reason is kept for the proposer, in `grants proposals`)
delulu grants    auto-approve --parent g_ID [--ttl 1h]   (approves, under the standing node g_ID, every pending proposal
whose mint is within it, and leaves each other one pending with what it adds beyond the node; never
guarded authority — it takes no owner code; exit 1 when one is left pending)
[--json]  (every grants verb)

commands.name: guard
usage: delulu guard     status | policy [show | set <class:pattern> <tier> | unset <class:pattern>] | bypass on|off  [--owner CODE]
delulu guard     request <g_ID> --use <class:pattern>.. --why ".." | pending | permits [revoke <id> --owner CODE]
delulu guard     approve <req-id> --owner CODE [--ttl D] [--uses N] [--comment ".."] | deny <req-id> --owner CODE --comment ".."
[--json]  (every guard verb)

commands.name: broker
usage: delulu broker    start [--foreground] [--dangerously-bypass-guard] [--guard-policy F] [--require-anchored-roots ANCHOR] | status | stop | rotate-key
[--json]

commands.name: sandbox
usage: delulu sandbox   status [--json]   (what this host can actually confine a guest with, from a real launch, and the
sandbox lifecycle records in this machine's audit chain — read-only, and it writes nothing)
delulu sandbox   probe [--json]   (which isolation levels this host can give a program, L0-L4, and for each
absent one the first missing prerequisite — every line an attempt, never a version string)
delulu sandbox   policy <file.delulu> [--sandbox-profile dev|contained|hostile-agent] [--json]
(what confinement a run WOULD have, without running: the limits, the mode, the policy hash,
and whether the channel can carry this program's surface at all)
delulu sandbox   policy <file.delulu> --format openshell [--grant K[=V]].. [--workdir DIR] [--binary PATH]
[--run-as ID[:ID]] [--json]   (PS-E-05: the OpenShell policy for running `delulu run` in its sandbox,
derived from the program's authority and grants and never wider than both; every grant accounted for)
delulu sandbox   require (--break-glass-key HEX.. | --no-break-glass) | release --break-glass TICKET
(PS-B-06: the operator requires the sandbox for every program `delulu` runs on this host;
only a ticket signed by a pinned key lets one program past it, or takes the policy off)
delulu sandbox   ticket --key SEED (--program FILE | --release) --ttl 15m --reason TEXT [--out FILE]
(mint a break-glass ticket, wherever the private key is — not on the host it is for)
delulu sandbox   attest --key SEED --attester NAME --guarantee TEXT.. [--measure-launcher FILE] -- COMMAND..
(PS-D-02: a SOFTWARE attester, run as an external launcher: signs the statement over the run's
nonce, writes it where the host asked, then becomes COMMAND — it says what its key's holder says;
a `--guarantee PROPERTY:HOW` vouches for one of the five boundary properties, as hostile-agent needs;

usage: delulu fleet     <verb>                              (fleet-level device/lease operations — see `delulu fleet` for the verb list)
update <artifact> --members N --approved F --previous H [--fail-health-at I] [--json]

usage: delulu secrets   set NAME VALUE | list [--state-dir DIR] [--json]  (broker-resident secrets)

usage: delulu locale    add <file.dpx> [--yes] | remove <name> | list [--json]   (catalog plugins: verified-class, ZERO authority, prose only)

usage: delulu morph     list | info <id> | check <file.toml> | render <file> (--to <id> | --to-canonical) [--json]

usage: delulu explain   <DLxxxx | E-REVOKE | E-GUARD | E-ATLAS | E-PALETTE | E-PLUGIN | E-ACTOR | E-SANDBOX> [--json]

usage: delulu examples  [--json]   (the shipped example programs — each checks, with the authority report

commands.name: device
usage: delulu device    sim [--seed N] [--actuator DEVICE:dim=lo..hi,heartbeat_ms=N,ttl_ms=N,fail=F]... [--sensor NAME]... [--json]
